text: Domestic policy

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In January 2023 Vance advocated for the U.S. Department of Justice to enforce the Comstock Act of 1873 to ban the mailing of drugs that induce abortion .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In June 2024 , the Supreme Court at least temporarily preserved access to mifepristone , after which Trump said during a debate that he " agree [ d ] with their decision " and would not " block " the drug .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In July , a week before Vance was announced as Trump 's running mate , Vance told NBC 's Meet the Press that he likewise supported access to mifepristone .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance also signed a letter to Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra requesting the withdrawal of a privacy rule preventing law enforcement from accessing abortion related health records .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In August 2024 , Vance was interviewed by Laura Ingraham , who brought up that suburban women are worried that abortion could be banned nationwide .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He responded : " I do n't buy that ... I think most suburban women care about the normal things most Americans care about right now . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance also said that , if Congress passed a national abortion ban , Trump would and should veto it .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: During the October 1 , 2024 , vice - presidential nominees ' debate , Vance said he " never supported a national ban " on abortion , despite having said in 2022 that he " certainly would like abortion to be illegal nationally " and pledging during his 2022 Senate campaign to " end abortion " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Economic policy Vance 's economic views in the Senate have been described as " economic populism " and sometimes " economic nationalism " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: This view has elements of protectionism , particularly with regard to re-shoring of American industry , especially manufacturing , and protecting American jobs more generally .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance has also expressed openness to a weaker U.S. dollar as a reserve currency , in order for American exports to be more competitive with other markets .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: His economic views are considered unorthodox in the Republican Party .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He supports tariffs and antitrust policy .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: His open support for striking auto workers , in particular , surprised many in the party .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: While Vance has indicated opposition to tax increases overall , he supports increases for certain taxes on university endowments , corporate mergers , and large multinationals .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He supports increasing the minimum wage and is highly skeptical of the economic and social contributions of large corporations .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance has expressed concern that large tech companies have too much influence in politics and the flow of information and has called to " break up "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Google , as well as implying he believes Meta should be split up .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He has said that Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) chair Lina Khan is " doing a pretty good job " , citing her antitrust enforcement against tech firms .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance and Senator Sheldon Whitehouse introduced the Stop Subsidizing Giant Mergers Act , which would end tax - free treatment for corporate mergers and acquisitions of companies above a certain threshold .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In September 2024 , Vance visited a Reading , Pennsylvania supermarket , where he complained that " a dozen eggs will cost you around $ 4 " and blamed Kamala Harris for it .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Video of Vance 's visit showed that the store 's price tag for a dozen eggs was under $ 3 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Labor unions Vance has regularly framed himself as a union ally , even going so far as to explicitly support labor in the 2023 United Auto Workers strike , which many in his party criticized .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Despite this , his legislative record has been criticized by some union leaders .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance also opposes the PRO Act , which expands protections related to employees ' rights to organize and collectively bargain , instead voicing support for proposals by the conservative group American Compass , which includes workers ' councils and sectoral bargaining .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Based on his voting record in the Senate , the AFL - CIO has scored him at 0 % on its Legislative Scorecard .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: On the other hand , Teamsters President Sean O'Brien has praised Vance and other Republicans for " listening to unions and standing up to corporations " , for which O'Brien was criticized by other union leaders , including from within the AFL - CIO and the Teamsters union itself .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance has criticized " right - to - work " anti-trade union laws .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: AFL - CIO president and Democratic Party lobbyist Liz Shuler has said : " A Trump – Vance administration would be a dream for corporate CEOs but a nightmare for workers .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Sen . JD Vance likes to pose as a union supporter on the picket line , but his record proves to be a sham .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He has introduced legislation to allow bosses to bypass their workers ' unions with phony corporate - run unions , disparaged striking UAW members while collecting hefty donations from one of the major auto companies , and opposed the landmark Protecting the Right to Organize ( PRO ) Act , which would end union - busting ' right to work ' laws and make it easier for workers to form unions and win strong contracts . "

text: Social Security Vance said in 2024 that he opposed cuts to Social Security or Medicare , and opposed privatizing Social Security .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He has said concerns about the long - term solvency of the Social Security Trust Fund are overstated , and that increasing labor force participation and birth rate would sustain the system .

text: Immigration and border security

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In 2023 , Vance introduced a bill that would make English the United States ' official language .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In September 2024 , Vance said " Haitian illegal immigrants " were " draining social services and generally causing chaos all over Springfield , Ohio .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Reports now show that people have had their pets abducted and eaten by people who should n't be in this country " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Both the Springfield city manager and the Springfield police responded that " there have been no credible reports or specific claims of pets being harmed , injured or abused by individuals within the immigrant community " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Springfield authorities also said , " Haitian immigrants are here legally , under the Immigration Parole Program " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance then said that it was " possible , of course , that all of these rumors will turn out to be false " , but also told his supporters : " Keep the cat memes flowing . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: After Vance 's claim about Haitians eating pets was disputed , he said : " Do you know what ’s confirmed ?

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: That a child was murdered by a Haitian migrant who had no right to be here . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: The child 's father responded : " My son , Aiden Clark , was not murdered .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He was accidentally killed by an immigrant from Haiti . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Aiden died in an accidental vehicular collision .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: His father accused " morally bankrupt politicians ... JD Vance and Donald Trump " of using Aiden 's " death for political gain " , saying " This needs to stop now " , and wishing that " the incessant group of hate - spewing people would leave us alone " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance also alleged a " massive rise in communicable diseases " in Springfield , but Clark County 's health commissioner reported having " not seen a substantial increase in all reportable communicable diseases " and that non-COVID reportable communicable diseases were lower in 2023 than anytime since 2016 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Later that month , Vance promoted conservative activist Christopher Rufo 's allegation that African migrants were eating cats in Dayton , Ohio , and criticized Kamala Harris and the media , calling the allegation " another ' debunked ' story that turned out to have merit " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: The allegation was based on an August 2023 video of skinned animals being grilled , which drew comments that the animals resembled chickens .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Dayton police responded , " there is no evidence to even remotely suggest that any group , including our immigrant community , is engaged in eating pets " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Dayton Mayor Jeffrey Mims reported " absolutely zero reports of this type of activity " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance continued to defend his claim that Haitian migrants eat cats , saying he was willing " to create stories so that the American media actually pays attention … we 're creating a story , meaning we 're creating the American media focusing on it . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Although many Haitian migrants were legal immigrants with temporary protected status , Vance said that since the Biden administration 's " border policy [ is ] a disgrace … I 'm still going to call [ the migrants ] illegal aliens . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In September 2023 , Vance introduced his " Freedom to Breathe " bill to prevent federal agencies from requiring masks on commercial airlines , on public transit , and in public schools , and to prevent those industries from refusing to serve people who do n't wear a mask .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He claimed that mask mandates " failed to control the spread of respiratory viruses " , " violated basic bodily freedom " , and were " unscientific " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In Senate remarks , he said children " need us to not be Chicken Little about every single respiratory pandemic and problem that confronts this country " .

text: Foreign policy

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: International organizations

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: At the 2024 Munich Security Conference , Vance said the U.S. did not want to pull out of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization ( NATO ) , but argued the U.S. should shift its focus to East Asia , and that certain European and NATO member countries were not spending enough for their own security .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: China Vance called China " the biggest threat " to the U.S. and argued that the war in Ukraine is distracting the U.S. from focusing on the threat from China .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He believes that China is the source of many American problems .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He has said that the U.S. is " flooded with cheap Chinese goods , with cheap foreign labor and , in the decades to come , deadly Chinese fentanyl " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: At the Munich Security Conference in 2024 , Vance said U.S. foreign policy should pivot from Europe to East Asia : " The United States has to focus more on East Asia .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: That is going to be the future of U.S. foreign policy for the next 40 years , and Europe has to wake up to that fact . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In December 2024 , responding to a post by Foundation for Defense of Democracies fellow Ivana Stradner criticizing Elon Musk 's support for the far - right Alternative for Germany ( AfD ) party , Vance sarcastically replied by saying " It ’s so dangerous for people to control their borders .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: So so dangerous .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: The dangerous level is off the charts " and continued by saying " I wonder how much money this person ’s employer gets from the American taxpayer ? " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In January 2025 , he said that while he is " not endorsing a party in the German elections " , he said an article by Musk titled Only the AfD Can Save Germany was " interesting " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He also claimed while American media " slanders AfD as Nazi - lite " , the party " is most popular in the same areas of Germany that were most resistant to the Nazis . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Israel Vance is a strong supporter of Israel and has said " culturally , morally , politically , it is a real ally in the sense that we 're not just sort of sharing interests , we 're actually sharing common values . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance has been called a " steadfast supporter of Israel throughout the country 's war in Gaza " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He supports U.S. funding Israel in the Gaza war .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He has said that Israel should win and end the war in Gaza " as quickly as possible " to enable the " Israelis and the Sunni Arab states " to form a united front against Iran .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance has criticized the Biden administration for " depriving the Israelis of the precision - guided weapons " the country needs , and said that Hamas bears full responsibility for all civilian deaths .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He criticized Biden in April 2024 for " micromanaging " Israeli actions in the war , saying , " you 've got to , first of all , enable Israel to actually finish the job " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance repeated his criticism of the Biden administration in July 2024 , saying : " Number one , you want Israel to get this war over and as quickly as possible because the longer it goes on , the harder their situation becomes .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: But second , after the war you want to reinvigorate that peace process between Israel , Saudi Arabia , the Jordanians , and so forth " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: More broadly , he has said , " We want the Israelis and the Sunnis to police their own region of the world . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In an October 2024 interview , Vance said : " Israel has the right to defend itself , but America 's interest is sometimes going to be distinct .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Sometimes we 're going to have overlapping interests and sometimes we 're going to have distinct interests .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: And our interest , I think , very much is in not going to war with Iran . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: When asked in October 2023 whether he would support military action against Iran after militias allegedly connected to Iran attacked U.S. troops , Vance said it would be a " mistake " , citing concern about significant escalation .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: After his nomination as Trump 's running mate , Vance praised the 2020 assassination of Iranian general Qasem Soleimani , adding : " If you 're gon na punch the Iranians , punch them hard . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In a 2024 speech , Vance said that " in 2003 , I made the mistake of supporting the Iraq War " , which he had served in as a combat correspondent in the Marine Corps , but that he later realized " that I had been lied to that the promises of the foreign policy establishment were a complete joke . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Russia – Ukraine war

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In a 2022 interview with Steve Bannon days before the Russian invasion of Ukraine , Vance said , " I do n't really care what happens to Ukraine one way or the other .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: I do care about the fact that in my community right now the leading cause of death among 18 - to 45 - year - olds is Mexican fentanyl that 's coming across the southern border . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance is a vocal critic of U.S. military aid to Ukraine in the ongoing Russo – Ukrainian War and has faced bipartisan criticism for that view .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In February 2024 , he said , " Given the realities that we face , the very real constraints in munitions and [ Ukraine 's ] manpower , what is reasonable to accomplish and when do we actually think we 're going to accomplish it ?

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: And my argument is , look , I think what 's reasonable to accomplish is some negotiated peace . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In April 2024 , Vance voted against an aid package for Ukraine ; in a New York Times essay , he wrote that he remained " opposed to virtually any proposal for the United States to continue funding this war " and argued that U.S. aid would not change the trajectory of the war .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He argues that Ukraine should adopt a " defensive strategy " to " preserve its precious military manpower , stop the bleeding and provide time for negotiations to commence " ; that the U.S. and Ukraine must " accept that Mr. Zelensky 's stated goal for the war — a return to 1991 boundaries — is fantastical " ; and that " Ukraine is going to have to cede some territory to the Russians " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In December 2023 , Vance was criticized for calling for the suspension of further aid to Ukraine because he said it would be used so its ministers " can buy a bigger yacht " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: He has criticized the Ukrainian government for corruption , and contends that the Biden administration has not properly audited aid to Ukraine .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In interviews and statements in 2024 , Vance said that he did not want Russia to conquer Ukraine , but supported a " freeze " of " the territorial lines somewhere close to where they are right now " ; guarantees of Kyiv 's neutrality and exclusion of Ukraine from NATO ( a key Russian demand ) ; and providing " some American security assistance over the long term . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance and Trump 's special envoy Keith Kellogg said that continued arms shipments to Ukraine and a heavily fortified demilitarised zone would ensure that Russia would not launch another invasion .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: United Kingdom

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: In July 2024 , after the British Labour Party won a landslide victory in the 2024 United Kingdom general election , Vance said in a speech at the National Conservatism Convention : " I was talking with a friend recently ... what is the first truly Islamist country that will get a nuclear weapon ?

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: And we were like , ' maybe it 's Iran , maybe Pakistan already kind of counts ' , and then we sort of finally decided maybe it 's actually the UK , since Labour just took over " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Senior British officials , such as Angela Rayner , James Murray , and Andrew Bowie dismissed this statement , which echoed right - wing characterizations of Britain and Europe .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Nevertheless , Vance and British foreign secretary David Lammy have described each other as friends , and Vance 's foreign policy advisor , Elbridge Colby , called Lammy " far preferable " to his Conservative predecessor , David Cameron .

text: Resignation and replacement in the U.S. Senate

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Republican nominee , Donald Trump selected Senator JD Vance to be his running mate in the 2024 United States presidential election , and Vance accepted .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Vance was elected the 50th Vice President of the United States in an election .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate career of JD Vance

text: Due to his and then - former President Donald Trump 's victory in the 2024 presidential election , Vance announced on January 9 , 2025 his plan to resign his Senate seat , effective January 10 .

text: The Committee Study of the Central Intelligence Agency 's Detention and Interrogation Program is a report compiled by the bipartisan United States Senate Select Committee on Intelligence ( SSCI ) about the Central Intelligence Agency ( CIA ) 's Detention and Interrogation Program and its use of torture during interrogation on detainees in CIA custody .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The report covers CIA activities before , during , and after the " war on terror " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The initial report was approved on December 13 , 2012 , by a vote of 9 – 6 , with seven Democrats , one independent , and one Republican voting in favor of the report and six Republicans voting in opposition .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The more than 6,700 - page report ( including 38,000 footnotes ) details the history of the CIA 's Detention and Interrogation Program and the Committee 's 20 findings and conclusions .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: On December 9 , 2014 , the SSCI released a 525 - page portion that consisted of key findings and an executive summary of the full report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: It took more than five years to complete .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The full unredacted report remains classified .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The report details actions by CIA officials including torturing prisoners , providing misleading or false information about classified CIA programs to the president , Department of Justice , Congress , and the media , impeding government oversight and internal criticism , and mismanaging the program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: It also revealed the existence of previously unknown detainees , that more detainees were subjected to " enhanced interrogation techniques " ( widely understood to be a euphemism for torture ) than was previously disclosed , and that more techniques were used without Department of Justice approval .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: It concluded that the use of enhanced interrogation techniques did not yield unique intelligence that saved lives ( as the CIA claimed ) , nor was it useful in gaining cooperation from detainees , and that the program damaged the United States ' international standing .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Some people , including some CIA officials and U.S. Republicans , disputed the report 's conclusions and said it provided an incomplete picture of the program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Others criticized the publishing of the report , citing its potential for damage to the U.S. and the contentious history of its development .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Former Republican presidential nominee John McCain praised the release of the report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Upon the report 's release , then - president Barack Obama stated , " One of the strengths that makes America exceptional is our willingness to openly confront our past , face our imperfections , make changes and do better . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: In the wake of the release of the report 's executive summary , a large number of individuals and organizations called for the prosecution of the CIA and government officials who perpetrated , approved , or provided legal cover for the torture of detainees ; however , prosecutions are considered unlikely .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The U.S. has also passed legislation , sponsored by Senators McCain and Dianne Feinstein , to prevent U.S. agencies from using many of the torture techniques described in the report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The 2019 film The Report covers the decade - long time period that led to the final creation and publication of the report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Impetus for the report

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: California Senator Dianne Feinstein said that the initial investigation began after press reports emerged stating that in 2005 , CIA Director of the National Clandestine Service Jose Rodriguez destroyed almost 100 video recordings of interrogations over objections from CIA and White House legal staff .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The tapes showed CIA officers and contractors using torture techniques such as waterboarding on detainees Abu Zubaydah and Abd al - Rahim al - Nashiri .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA did not inform the United States Senate Select Committee on Intelligence ( SSCI ) that Rodriguez had destroyed the tapes , and the committee had not known they had existed .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: SSCI believed that Rodriguez was covering up illegal activities by the CIA , although the committee had initially been told by CIA officials that Rodriguez was not engaging in " destruction of evidence " .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Rodriguez preemptively criticized the report in an op-ed for The Washington Post on December 5 , 2014 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: In addition to destroying the torture tapes , the Committee 's report shows that Rodriguez was heavily involved in the CIA 's use of torture , including overseeing black sites where torture took place , preventing CIA Counterterrorism Center ( CTC ) legal staff from implementing vetting processes for interrogators , provided misleading information to the Department of Defense about a detainee 's identity , and participated in the payment of millions of dollars to a country hosting a black site .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: CIA Director Michael Hayden told the Committee on December 11 , 2007 , that if the Committee had asked for the videos , the CIA would have provided them , and offered the Committee written summaries of the interrogation sessions depicted on the destroyed tapes .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: CIA records show that the decision to destroy the tapes came shortly after CIA attorneys raised concerns about Congress discovering the tapes ' existence .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Jane Mayer 's book The Dark Side stated that the CIA also neglected to inform the 9/11 Commission that these tapes existed : " In a meeting on December 23 , 2003 , [ Commission executive director Philip D. ]

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Zelikow demanded that the CIA at the very least provide any and all documents responsive to its requests , even if the Commission had not specifically asked for them .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: [ CIA Director George ]

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Tenet replied by alluding to several documents he thought would be helpful .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: But in an omission that would later become part of a criminal investigation , neither Tenet nor anyone else from the CIA in the meeting mentioned that , in fact , the Agency had in its possession at that point hundreds of hours of videotapes of the interrogations of Abu Zubayda and Abd al - Rahim al - Nashiri , both of whom were waterboarded . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: In December 2007 , the committee opened an investigation into the tape destruction and designated four staffers to conduct the investigation , which they completed around early 2009 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Development of the report On February 11 , 2009 , the committee began considering a broader review of the CIA 's detention and interrogation practices after committee staff presented a summary of the operational cables detailing the interrogations of Abu Zubaydah and Abd al - Rahim al - Nashiri .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: On March 5 , 2009 , the Senate Intelligence Committee voted 14 – 1 to open an investigation into the CIA detention and interrogation program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: In August 2009 , Attorney General Eric Holder announced a parallel preliminary criminal investigation into the use of unauthorized interrogation techniques by CIA officials .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: As a result of the attorney general 's investigation , the Republican minority on the SSCI concluded that many witnesses were unlikely to participate in the investigation for fear of criminal liability .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Citing the attorney general investigation as their reason , the Republican minority of the SSCI withdrew their participation from the investigation in September 2009 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The Senate investigation was led by Committee staffer and former FBI investigator Daniel J. Jones , and was prepared following a review of more than 6.3 million pages of documents , cables , emails , and other materials principally provided by the CIA .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The document production phase lasted more than three years and was completed in July 2012 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: As described in the Senate report , an additional 9,400 classified documents repeatedly requested by the SSCI were withheld by the White House under a claim of executive privilege .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Despite the initial expectation that interviews would be used , no formal interviews or hearings were conducted in the preparation of the report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The lack of interviews and hearings was one of the chief complaints of the Republican minority on SSCI .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: However , the report included CIA officials ' on - the - record statements in classified committee hearings , written statements , and interviews conducted through the CIA Inspector General 's office and the Agency 's oral history program , as well as through the formal response to the committee in June 2013 after reading the report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: These statements and interviews included those from CIA director George Tenet , CTC director Jose Rodriguez , CIA general counsel Scott Muller , CIA deputy director of operations James Pavitt , CIA acting general counsel John Rizzo , CIA deputy director John McLaughlin , and a variety of interrogators , lawyers , medical personnel , senior counterterrorism analysts and managers of the detention and interrogation program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA estimated that approximately $ 40 million in personnel time and resources was spent assisting the investigation , but this was largely because of the CIA 's insistence on hiring Centra Technology contractors to review documents prior to presenting them to the Committee and establishing a separate secure facility and computer network for CIA and Committee staff to use during the review .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: This deviated from the standard document - sharing process , in which the CIA provides documents for Committee staff to review in Committee offices .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The final report was approved on December 13 , 2012 , by a vote of 9 – 6 , with eight Democrats and one Republican ( Olympia Snowe ) voting in favor of publication and six Republicans voting in opposition , and the published minority views of Senator Chambliss were joined by Senators Burr , Risch , Coats , Rubio , and Coburn .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Republican Senator John McCain , a member of the Committee ex officio , did not have a vote , but he supported approval alongside Snowe .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: On April 3 , 2014 , the SSCI voted 11 – 3 to submit a revised version of the executive summary , findings , and recommendations of the report for declassification analysis in preparation for future public release .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Independent Senator Angus King and Republican Senator Susan Collins supported the release of the report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: After eight months , involving contentious negotiations about what details should remain classified , the revised executive summary , findings , and recommendations were made public with many redactions on December 9 , 2014 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA had demanded that the Committee redact the names of all detainees , all CIA officer 's pseudonyms , and the names of all countries that hosted black sites .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Daniel J. Jones told The Guardian that the Agency wanted to redact other material , such as references to Allah .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA wanted pseudonyms to be used for contractors and interrogators James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen , despite the fact that they had both been identified publicly prior to the report 's release .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The report ended up including detainee names , and used pseudonyms ( such as " CIA OFFICER 1 " ) for several Agency officers , but redacted the names of almost all others , as well as black site host countries .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Information about the cooperation of foreign agencies with the CIA has been redacted from the report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The British chairman of the Intelligence and Security Committee stated they would request access to anything taken out of the report at the request of British agencies .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Panetta Review and CIA hacking incident

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: On December 17 , 2013 , Sen. Mark Udall ( D - CO ) revealed the existence of a secret internal review ( the " Panetta Review " ) conducted by the CIA that was consistent with the Senate 's report but conflicted with the CIA 's official response to the report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: In January 2014 , CIA officials claimed that the Intelligence Committee had accessed portions of the " Panetta Review " and removed them from CIA facilities in 2010 without CIA authorization .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: In March 2014 , Sen. Dianne Feinstein ( D - CA ) , chairwoman of the Intelligence Committee , confirmed that a portion of the " Panetta Review " had been copied and transferred to a safe in the Senate 's Hart Office Building .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: She stated that the action was necessary to protect the documents from the CIA , which had destroyed videotapes depicting brutal interrogation methods in 2005 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: During the review process the CIA had removed hundreds of pages of documents from the Committee staff 's CIA - provided computer network ( called " RDINet " for " rendition , detention , and interrogation " ) without informing Committee staff .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: According to Senator Feinstein , when Committee staff inquired about the missing documents , CIA staff initially denied the files had been removed , then blamed IT contractors , and finally falsely claimed that the White House had requested their removal .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: When negotiating the review process , the Committee and the CIA came to an agreement that the CIA would establish " a walled - off network share - drive " accessible only to Committee staff , and that " CIA access to the walled off network shared drive will be limited to CIA information technology staff , except as authorized by the committee or its staff . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: During an " extraordinary " 45 - minute speech on March 11 , 2014 , Feinstein said the CIA unlawfully searched the Intelligence Committee 's computers to determine how the committee staff obtained the " Panetta Review " documents .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Feinstein also said that the CIA 's acting general counsel , later identified as Robert Eatinger , requested the FBI conduct a criminal inquiry into the committee staff who had accessed and relocated the " Panetta Review " documents .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: She said she believed that the request was " a potential effort to intimidate [ Intelligence Committee ] staff . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Eatinger had been involved in the destruction of video tapes in 2005 ( which started the Senate investigation ) , and Feinstein added that Eatinger was mentioned by name over 1,600 times in the Committee 's full report .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The same day that Feinstein made the allegations , CIA director John O. Brennan denied that the CIA searched the Senate computers , stating , " As far as the allegations of , you know , CIA hacking into , you know , Senate computers , nothing could be further from the truth .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: I mean we would n't do that .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: I mean that 's just beyond the – you know , the scope of reason in terms of what we would do ...

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: When the facts come out on this , I think a lot of people who are claiming that there has been this tremendous sort of spying and monitoring and hacking will be proved wrong . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: On July 31 , 2014 , the CIA 's Inspector General confirmed that the CIA had improperly gained access to and searched the Senate Intelligence Committee 's computer network , including that CIA employees had accessed the Committee 's computers , read Committee staff 's email , and sent a criminal referral to the Department of Justice based on false information .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: A Justice Department spokesman later announced that they would not be pursuing charges in the hacking incident .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: An internal review panel appointed by Brennan contended that the searches " were lawful and in some cases done at the behest of John O. Brennan , the C.I.A. director . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Findings listed in the report

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The more - than 6,700 - page report produced 20 key findings .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: They are , verbatim from the unclassified Executive Summary report :

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA 's use of its enhanced interrogation techniques was not an effective means of acquiring intelligence or gaining cooperation from detainees .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA 's justification for the use of its enhanced interrogation techniques rested on inaccurate claims of their effectiveness .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The interrogations of CIA detainees were brutal and far worse than the CIA represented to policymakers and others .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The conditions of confinement for CIA detainees were harsher than the CIA had represented to policymakers and others .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA repeatedly provided inaccurate information to the Department of Justice ( DOJ ) , impeding a proper legal analysis of the CIA 's Detention and Interrogation Program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA has actively avoided or impeded congressional oversight of the program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA impeded effective White House oversight and decision - making .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA 's operation and management of the program complicated , and in some cases impeded , the national security missions of other Executive Branch agencies .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA impeded oversight by the CIA 's Office of Inspector General .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA coordinated the release of classified information to the media , including inaccurate information concerning the effectiveness of the CIA 's enhanced interrogation techniques .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA was unprepared as it began operating its Detention and Interrogation Program more than six months after being granted detention authorities .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA 's management and operation of its Detention and Interrogation Program was deeply flawed throughout the program 's duration , particularly so in 2002 and early 2003 .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Two contract psychologists devised the CIA 's enhanced interrogation techniques and played a central role in the operation , assessments , and management of the CIA 's Detention and Interrogation Program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: By 2005 , the CIA had overwhelmingly outsourced operations related to the program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: CIA detainees were subjected to coercive interrogation techniques that had not been approved by the Department of Justice or had not been authorized by CIA Headquarters .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA did not conduct a comprehensive or accurate accounting of the number of individuals it detained , and held individuals who did not meet the legal standard for detention .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA 's claims about the number of detainees held and subjected to its enhanced interrogation techniques were inaccurate .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA failed to adequately evaluate the effectiveness of its enhanced interrogation techniques .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA rarely reprimanded or held personnel accountable for serious or significant violations , inappropriate activities , and systematic and individual management failures .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA marginalized and ignored numerous internal critiques , criticisms , and objections concerning the operation and management of the CIA 's Detention and Interrogation Program .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA 's Detention and Interrogation Program was inherently unsustainable and had effectively ended by 2006 due to unauthorized press disclosures , reduced cooperation from other nations , and legal and oversight concerns .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA 's Detention and Interrogation Program damaged the United States ' standing in the world , and resulted in other significant monetary and non-monetary costs .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Findings as reported by media outlets

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Examples of torture and abuse of prisoners

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA had force - fed some prisoners orally and / or anally in order to establish " total control over the detainee . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The report notes that CIA documents indicate " Chief of Interrogations [ redacted ] also ordered the rectal rehydration of KSM without a determination of medical need , a procedure that the chief of interrogations would later characterize as illustrative of the interrogator ’s ' total control over the detainee . ' "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The Committee found that " [ a ] t least five CIA detainees were subjected to ' rectal rehydration ' or rectal feeding without documented medical necessity . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: These detainees are listed as Abu Zubaydah , Khalid Shaykh Mohammad , Majid Khan , and Marwan al - Jabbur .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: At least one prisoner was " diagnosed with chronic hemorrhoids , an anal fissure and symptomatic rectal prolapse , " symptoms normally associated with a violent rape .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The report identified this detainee as Mustafa al - Hawsawi .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: CIA officials , including general counsel Scott Miller and deputy director of operations James Pavitt , were told that rectal exams of at least two prisoners had been conducted with " excessive force . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: A CIA attorney was asked to follow up on these incidents , but the report states that " CIA records do not indicate any resolution of the inquiry . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: CIA interrogators threatened to rape and murder children and / or family members of prisoners .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: For example , according to the CIA 's Inspector General , a CIA interrogator told Abd al - Rahim al - Nashiri that if he did not provide information , " We could get your mother in here , " and " We can bring your family in here . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The interrogator also led al - Nashiri to believe that he was being held in a Middle Eastern country whose interrogators sexually abused female family members in front of detainees .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: In November 2002 the CIA killed Gul Rahman during interrogation by hypothermia .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Rahman was tortured by CIA officers and contractors and left wearing only a sweatshirt , chained to a wall in a seating position on a cold floor .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: No CIA employees were disciplined as a result of his death , and the CIA officer who managed the black site where Rahman died , who was not a trained interrogator and had a history of behavioral issues , was recommended for a cash award of $ 2,500 for " consistently superior work " and continued to interrogate detainees .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: At least four prisoners with injuries to their legs ( two with broken feet , one with a sprained ankle and one with an amputated leg ) were forced to stand on their injuries .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Interrogators subjected these detainees to extended periods of standing sleep deprivation without prior headquarters approval .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Interrogators told prisoners that they would be killed .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: For example : one prisoner , Abu Zubaydah , was told " We can never let the world know what I have done to you " , another was told that the only way he would be allowed to leave the prison would be in a coffin - shaped confinement box .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: One CIA interrogator who was subsequently sent home early threatened prisoner Abd al - Rahim al - Nashiri with a gun and power drill , racking a handgun and revving the drill next to al - Nashiri 's hooded head .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The interrogator had not sought Headquarters approval for these unauthorized actions .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: At least two prisoners were victims of " mock executions . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: According to the CIA 's Inspector General , the same debriefer who used the gun and drill on al - Nashiri claimed that he had witnessed other CIA interrogators stage an execution to scare a detainee , and several other CIA officers also said that they had witnessed or participated in mock executions .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Several prisoners almost died and became completely unresponsive or nearly drowned during waterboarding .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Multiple CIA communications described CIA interrogators waterboarding Abu Zubaydah and in one session , Zubaydah " becoming completely unresponsive , with bubbles rising through his open , full mouth . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: He remained unresponsive until given medical attention , when he regained consciousness and expelled " copious amounts of liquid . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Abu Zubaydah 's eye was so badly damaged during his time in prison that it was surgically removed .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA kept some prisoners awake for over one week ( 180 hours ) , as well as shorter extended periods of time .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: This included the use of sitting or standing stress positions that prevented sleep .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Sleep deprivation caused at least five to experience " disturbing " hallucinations .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: The CIA claimed in its 2013 response that when detainees experienced hallucinations during sleep deprivation , medical staff intervened and allowed the detainee to sleep .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: However , CIA records indicate that this was not always true .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: After more than a month of torture , including loud music , dietary and temperature manipulation , sleep and sensory deprivation , and shackling , prisoner Ridha al - Najjar was psychologically traumatized to the point of being described as " a broken man . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Prisoners were forced to use buckets for toilets .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: As punishment , interrogators could remove the waste bucket from a prisoner 's cell .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: In one case , CIA interrogators told a detainee that he could earn a bucket by cooperating , and those undergoing standing sleep deprivation were routinely put in diapers .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: This contradicts CIA Director Michael Hayden 's assertion that " Detainees have never been denied the means – at a minimum , they 've always had a bucket – to dispose of their human waste . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: On visiting one of the CIA black sites , CIA records indicate that Federal Bureau of Prisons representatives stated " they [ had ] never been in a facility where individuals were so sensory deprived i.e. , constant white noise , no talking , everyone in the dark , with the guards wearing a light on their head when they collected and escorted a detainee to an interrogation cell , detainees constantly being shackled to the wall or floor , and the starkness of each cell ( concrete and bars ) .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: There is nothing like this in the Federal Bureau of Prisons .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: They then explained that they understood the mission and it was their collective assessment that in spite of all this sensory deprivation , the detainees were not being treated in humanely [ sic ] . "

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: This evaluation was of the same black site where Gul Rahman died after CIA interrogators beat him and left him shackled half nude on a cold floor .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Janat Gul was tortured for months based on false accusations made by an informant known as Asset Y.

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: According to CIA documents , senior CIA officers had expressed doubt about the source 's credibility and Gul denied having information about imminent threats to the United States , but interrogators proceeded to subject Gul to numerous torture techniques .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Even after CIA staff at the site stated that they believed Gul was not withholding information , CIA Headquarters ordered continued use of torture tactics .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: Gul never provided the information the CIA thought he possessed , and Asset Y admitted to fabricating the accusations against him .

source.page_title: U.S. Senate report on CIA torture

text: CIA interrogators forced detainee Abu Zubaydah into a box the size of a coffin for a total of 266 hours ( over 11 days ) and also forced him to stay for 29 hours in a box measuring 21 inches ( 53 cm ) wide , 2.5 feet ( 76 cm ) deep and 2.5 feet ( 76 cm ) high .

text: The U.S. Synchronized Skating Championships is an annual synchronized skating competition , sanctioned by U.S. Figure Skating , held to determine the national champions of the United States .
It was first held in 1984 .
Teams who qualify at a Sectional Championship competition compete in eight levels : juvenile , intermediate , novice , junior , senior , collegiate , adult and masters .

The top two senior teams then go on to compete at the World Synchronized Skating Championships , while at the Junior level the teams competing at the World Junior Synchronized Skating Championships is predetermined by a Junior World Qualifier competition .
The teams competing at the Junior Level at the U.S. Synchronized Skating Championships are competing for international assignment for the next years .
Name changes
When first held in 1984 , the competition was called the U.S. Precision Championships .
Subsequently , up to and including 1999 , this competition was called the U.S. Precision Team Skating ( Synchronized Skating ) Championships .
In 2000 , the name of the competition was changed to U.S. Synchronized Team Skating Championships .
In 2008 , the current name U.S. Synchronized Skating Championships was adopted .
Competitive Levels
The definitions for teams in each of the qualify levels are detailed below .
All events are judged under the ISU International Judging System ( IJS ) .
Juvenile : A team of 12 - 20 skaters .
Skaters must be under 13 and have passed the pre-juvenile moves in the field test .
Intermediate : A team of 12 - 20 skaters .
Skaters must be under 18 and have passed the juvenile moves in the field test .
Novice : A team of 12 - 20 skaters .
Skaters must be under 16 , with the exception of four skaters who may be 16 or 17 , and have passed the intermediate moves in the field test .
Junior : A team of 12 - 16 skaters .
Skaters must be at least 13 years old and under 19 .
All skaters must have passed the novice moves in the field test .
Senior : A team of 16 skaters .
Skaters must be at least 15 years old and have passed the junior moves in the field test .
Collegiate : A team of 12 - 20 skaters .
Skaters must be enrolled in a college or degree program as full - time students and have passed the juvenile moves in the field test .
Adult : A team or 12 - 20 skaters .
All skaters must be 18 years or older .
All skaters must have passed at least one of the following tests : preliminary moves in the field , adult bronze moves in the field , preliminary figure or preliminary dance .
Masters :
A team or 12 - 20 skaters .
All skaters must be 25 years or older .

U.S. Venture Partners ( USVP ) is a venture capital investment firm specializing in early - stage ventures in enterprise software , cybersecurity , consumer , e-commerce , healthcare , and IT - enabled healthcare services .
The venture capital partnership is headquartered in Menlo Park , California .
Since its inception in 1981 , USVP has invested over $ 4.3 billion across a wide range of sectors .
Out of the 524 companies financed by USVP , 93 have completed an initial public offering .

History Founded by Bill Bowes , Stuart Moldaw , and Robert Sackman , U.S. Venture Partners was an early entrant to the burgeoning venture capital industry in Silicon Valley in the late 1970s and early 1980s .
As of 2022 , the firm was investing out of its thirteenth fund , USVP XIII .

Composed of former venture investors , entrepreneurs , CEOs , technologists , corporate executives , financial professionals , and industry domain experts , USVP has a combined 150 years of investment and operating experience with backgrounds across a wide array of sectors .
The investment team is composed of Jacques Benkoski , Steve Krausz , Rick Lewis , Jonathan Root , Casey Tansey and Dafina Toncheva .
The firm makes investments between $ 5 million and $ 10 million in markets with revenue potential exceeding $ 1 billion .
USVP prefers to invest in companies with a market greater than $ 300 million and avoids companies in direct competition with each other .
On average , USVP will invest for a period of three to ten years .

The firm has invested across multiple sectors over the years and is focused on enterprise software , IT security , consumer internet , mobile , e-commerce , healthcare , and IT - enabled healthcare services .

The firm 's recent investments include Arkose Labs , Box , Carrot Fertility , Cato Networks , Happy Returns , HeartFlow , HotelTonight , Human Interest , Inari Medical , Inspire Medical Systems , Intersect ENT , Medigate , Omada Health , Pluto TV , ThreatMetrix , and Zerto .

Notable historical investments include : Sun Microsystems , Callaway Golf , St. Francis Medical , SanDisk , Ross Stores , Ask Jeeves , Adify , PetSmart , Check Point , Mellanox , Vontu , Proteolix , Dotomi , Imperva , Guidewire Software , Yammer , Trusteer , Nanostim and Trunk Club .
U.S. Xpress ( USX ) is an American trucking company headquartered in Chattanooga , Tennessee , that has operated as a subsidiary of Knight - Swift since 2023 .
The company offers truckload shipping and other transportation services across the United States .
U.S. Xpress was founded in 1985 by Max Fuller and Patrick Quinn .
The company went public in 1994 , selling 2.5 million shares of common stock .
It entered a period of growth in the following years , acquiring a number of transportation companies throughout the country .
By 1998 , U.S. Xpress was the fifth - largest publicly traded trucking firm in the United States , with a fleet of more than 4,500 vehicles .
U.S. Xpress returned to private ownership in 2007 , with Fuller and Quinn purchasing it from stockholders .
The company went public for a second time in 2018 , raising more than $ 250 million through the stock launch .
Investors later filed a lawsuit against the company , alleging that it failed to reveal information before the public offering that it was required to divulge under securities law .
On March 21 , 2023 , Knight - Swift Transportation Holdings , one of the largest truckload carriers in North America , announced an agreement to acquire U.S. Xpress for approximately $ 808 million .
As of 2025 , U.S. Xpress has a dedicated fleet of 2,000 trucks with 2,300 drivers .
The company operates eleven terminals across the United States .

The U.S. and Japan Mutual Defense Assistance Agreement was signed on March 8 , 1954 , in Tokyo between John Allison of the United States and Katsuo Okazaki of Japan .

source.page_title: U.S. and Japan Mutual Defense Assistance Agreement

text: The accord contained eleven articles and seven amendments ( or annexes ) .

source.page_title: U.S. and Japan Mutual Defense Assistance Agreement

text: The agreement dictated that both the United States and Japan support each other militarily .

source.page_title: U.S. and Japan Mutual Defense Assistance Agreement

text: Specifically , it permitted the United States to station its troops on Japanese soil in order to maintain security in the region .

source.page_title: U.S. and Japan Mutual Defense Assistance Agreement

text: Moreover , Japan was obligated to take responsibility in protecting itself and was permitted to rearm for defensive purposes only .

source.page_title: U.S. and Japan Mutual Defense Assistance Agreement

text: Ultimately , the agreement was ratified on May 1 , 1954 .

text: In the U.S. , critical infrastructure protection ( CIP ) is a concept that relates to the preparedness and response to serious incidents that involve the critical infrastructure of a region or the nation .
The American Presidential directive PDD - 63 of May 1998 set up a national program of " Critical Infrastructure Protection " .
In 2014 the NIST Cybersecurity Framework was published after further presidential directives .
History The U.S. CIP is a national program to ensure the security of vulnerable and interconnected infrastructures of the United States .
